question: to the Commission Emmanouil Fragkos (ECR) Subject:

Under the Treaty of Lausanne and the Montreux Convention Regarding the Regime of the Straits, the Bosphorus and the Dardanelles were meant to stay open to international shipping. This state of affairs was established in order to ensure freedom of transit between the Black Sea and the Mediterranean Sea, maintaining stability and the international equilibrium. As a trade-off for free shipping and as part of a geopolitical compromise, Imbros and Tenedos were given to Türkiye. Article 14 of the Treaty of Lausanne provided for a special autonomous status for the Greek population of the two islands, with a view to protecting the unique identity of the local culture and community. After the ‘ethnic cleansing’ committed against the people of Imbros and Tenedos, in recent years Türkiye has been beefing up shipping control mechanisms and going ahead with projects such as Kanal Istanbul, raising objections about the strengthening of unilateral controls in what is an international sea route. In view of the above and in the context of the EU-Türkiye negotiations, can the Commission say: 1.

Does it intend to consider the combined application of the Montreux Convention and the Treaty of Lausanne, pushing for the return of Imbros and Tenedos to Greece or at least for the restored rights of the expelled people of Imbros and Tenedos, their compensation and the drafting of an autonomy plan for the islands?
Could it consider a specific funding programme for the return of the expelled people of Imbros and Tenedos to their respective homelands?
If not, does it believe that the ethnic cleansing committed by Türkiye against the Greeks of Imbros and Tenedos does not concern it?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (1.7.2026)

The European Commission has highlighted, including in the 2025 enlargement report1, the persistent challenges facing the Greek minority in Türkiye. The Commission recalls that the recommendations set out in Resolution 1625 (2008) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe2 on the bicultural character of the islands of Gökçeada (Imbros) and Bozcaada (Tenedos) remain valid and unaddressed. The resolution calls for urgent action to restore minority schools, return expropriated properties and improve infrastructure, while safeguarding the rights of the Greek minority. The Commission also recalls that the Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe urged the Turkish authorities to implement the rulings of the European Court of Human Rights concerning the minority and property rights of the Greek minority on these two islands. The Commission supports these objectives and will continue to urge Türkiye to fulfil its obligations. It will also continue to encourage constructive dialogue with Greece and to promote reconciliation, restitution and respect for minority rights. The Commission will continue to monitor the situation and address these concerns in its bilateral contacts with the Turkish authorities.
